title: Learn to Park Ideas for Later
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses meeting digressions, arguing that off-topic remarks act like a hand grenade that derails a group's focus even after the discussion is nominally brought back on track. The recommended tool is a literal 'Parking Lot' — a flip chart or whiteboard where off-topic ideas get written down for later discussion instead of being addressed in the moment. The article notes that once teams grow accustomed to this device, the very presence of the Parking Lot deters people from digressing in the first place, since they know their idea will still be captured. It closes by reinforcing that keeping meetings on time and on track is a discipline best supported by a simple, visible tool rather than pure willpower.
points: Off-topic digressions derail productive discussions even after the group returns to the original topic.
A visible 'Parking Lot' (flip chart or whiteboard) captures off-topic ideas for later without losing them.
Teams that adopt the Parking Lot habit often digress less overall, since ideas are guaranteed to be revisited.
The tool works because it lets a leader redirect without dismissing the person's idea outright.
Keeping meetings on track is framed as a discipline best supported by simple visible tools, not willpower alone.
quotes: Some remarks and ideas can short-circuit an otherwise productive team discussion.
That’s why great leaders employ a Parking Lot, where off-topic ideas or comments can be parked and discussed later.
The very existence of a Parking Lot reminds team members not to digress if they can avoid it.
Any statement that redirects the discussion, however unintentional, is actually a hand grenade in disguise.
With only a little trial and error, team members quickly become used to this tactic.
Despite the best team’s effort, the group never recaptures the exact point being made prior to the diversion.
